The British law of 18 July 1947 that ended the Raj and created two independent states, India and Pakistan, on 15 August 1947.

On 20 February 1947 Prime Minister Clement Attlee told Parliament that Britain would leave India by June 1948. Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last viceroy, arrived in Delhi in March and decided to go sooner. His first scheme, Plan Balkan, would have let each province choose its fate. He showed it to Nehru at Simla in May, and Nehru rejected it, fearing India would break into many pieces.

The plan that went ahead, announced on 3 June, split India along religious lines and split Punjab and Bengal too. Jinnah, who had wanted all of both provinces, was forced to take a smaller "moth-eaten" Pakistan. The date was moved up to August.

The haste left little time to plan. The Radcliffe Line was drawn in weeks and the Partition was marked by mass killing and the flight of millions.
sum: The British law of 18 July 1947 that ended the Raj and created two independent states, India and Pakistan, on 15 August 1947.
